questions: Should the function treat numpy numeric types (e.g., np.int64, np.float32) as numeric values, or only Python int and float?

If a tuple contains more elements than others, should the missing positions in shorter tuples be filled with NaN (or ignored) for mean calculation, or should the function only consider positions present in at least one tuple?
Should the function handle nested iterables (like lists within tuples) as non-numeric, or attempt to recursively check for numbers inside them?
Is the index 'Position i' zero-indexed based on the maximum tuple length, or based on the order of positions as they appear (so Position 0 always corresponds to first element across tuples)?
Should the mean be computed as a floating-point number even if all numeric values are integers, or should it preserve integer type if possible?
If a position has a mix of numeric and non-numeric values, should the mean be calculated only from numeric values, ignoring non-numeric, as stated, or should non-numeric values cause an error?
Should the function treat boolean values (True/False) as numeric (since they subclass int in Python) or as non-numeric?
Is the output DataFrame required to have a specific column name exactly 'Mean Value' (case-sensitive) and index format exactly 'Position i' (with space), or are variations allowed?
